finding.problem: The new wording_only flag on Commit is only passed in as an optional param on record_commit. Nothing in the domain computes or verifies it. Any commit recorded with wording_only=true can be approved without a passing change check. The change check covers structure, semantics, scenarios, harness, past actions and stranded objects, and a wording edit can still break any of these. The bypass rests on an unchecked claim.
finding.where: authoring.domain.yaml: record_commit params/effects, approve_commit precondition checks-pass

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The wording_only flag is an unverified caller-supplied claim that bypasses the check; this is a real weakness of the edit but not the rule conflict itself.

finding.problem: A commit whose change check ran and failed (checks_passed=false) can still be approved if wording_only is true. The 'or' makes the flag override a recorded failure, in the approve_commit precondition, the record_approval precondition and the invariant. This is not just skipping a check that wasn't run.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: The 'or wording_only' clauses in all three places let a commit be approved without a passing change check, directly conflicting with the rule that approved commits passed their checks.

finding.problem: Three rules that were confirmed from the interview (checks-pass, approved-only-if-checked, approved-commits-passed-their-checks) were rewritten. Their interview source and confirmed status were removed and they are now 'proposed'. A weakening of an approval safeguard was made without a person's confirmation. The invariant and both preconditions are now unconfirmed pieces of a confirmed action.

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: It identifies the rewrite of the confirmed approval-requires-passing-check rule in all three places (precondition, record_approval, invariant), which is the seeded conflict.

finding.problem: Text that states the old guarantee is now false. The purpose announcement says 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed'. The glossary says the change check is 'The checks a commit runs before approval'. The Delivery announcement says 'Nothing that fails its checks or lacks a person's approval gets there'. Wording-only commits can now be approved, and so delivered, with no check or after a failed one.
finding.where: authoring.domain.yaml purpose.announcement and glossary 'change check'/'approval'; delivery.domain.yaml purpose.announcement

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Announcements and glossary text still assert that every change is checked and nothing failing gets delivered, which the edit makes false.

finding.problem: No scenario covers the new wording-only path, either approval without a check or a wording_only commit with a failed check. The existing scenario approve-only-after-a-passing-check only exercises the old path. The relaxed rule is untested. The world fixtures have no wording_only commit.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: No scenario or fixture covers the new wording-only approval path, so the relaxed rule is untested.

finding.problem: Approval behaviour changed and the Commit gained a new property, but the domain version (4) and the composition interface (1) were not changed. Delivery relies on approved commits having passed their checks, and that assumption is now broken without any signal.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Version and interface bump bookkeeping is speculative and not a concrete defect of the change; Delivery's assumption is the same rule conflict already covered.

edit.why: It adds a wording_only flag and lets approve_commit, record_approval and the invariant accept a commit that only changed wording without a passing change check.
